lede.t: In May 2026, the eventual winner of the Commonwealth Short Story Prize was accused of using AI to write their story.
Granta, the literary magazine that published the story, was widely mocked for the naivety of its investigation: it simply asked Claude whether AI had written the story.
In this paper, we show that Granta was not naive, but just a few months early.

Frontier models now identify AI text as well as specialized detectors like Pangram, and they go much further: given a single text, with no web search or list of candidates, they can often name the lab behind an AI-generated text, or even the specific person who wrote a human one.

cases_intro.t: A document's prose and ideas can each come from a person or an AI model, giving the following four cases:

cases.def: A person wrote the prose and came up with the ideas.
A person wrote, in their own words, from a model's ideas.
A model wrote the prose and came up with the ideas.
A person came up with the ideas, and a model wrote, rewrote, or polished the prose.

title.t: Model accuracy has improved over time.

steps.t: Accuracy on both labels climbed from 27% for GPT-4o in 2024 and 59% for GPT-5.2 in 2025 to 91% for present-day frontier models.
The best open-weight models still trail, with Kimi K3.1 Pro reaching 63%.
Frontier models are competitive with trained detectors such as Pangram 4 at prose detection.
On idea detection, they exceed the accuracy of IdeaLens, the only existing state-of-the-art idea detector.

steps.t: We create a dataset of short stories, news articles, and op-eds generated by 34 models from 11 labs.
Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5 and Argon can identify text from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google with 98% accuracy or more.
Moonshot's Kimi K3 is usually mistaken for Claude, and Alibaba's Qwen3.8 models for GPT.
Later reports name Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3, and date campaigns against Claude shortly before their release.

caption.t: Claude Fable 5.2 recognizes most texts from earlier Kimi and Qwen releases, but attributes nearly every Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3 text to Claude and most Qwen3.8 27B and Grok 4.7 texts to GPT.

OpenAI.name: GPT
OpenAI.t: GPT hedges its claims, flags gaps instead of inventing specifics, and leans on aphorisms.

Anthropic.name: Claude
Anthropic.t: Claude treats opposing views charitably, writes with dry wit, and ends quietly.

Google.name: Gemini
Google.t: Gemini stacks adjectives and piles on intensifiers and stock clichés, and invents named sources and quotes in its news articles.
